post.text:
WE GET A SAY. 🗳️

The last 24h in superintelligence:
- Data centres lost nearly every local US vote
- Tencent's new AI can see and use a computer
- AMD's data centre sales nearly doubled
- 6 robots ran a Shanghai store for 24h

Would you trust a robot barista?
post.alt: A 3-minute, fast-cut motion-graphics showreel of the last day in superintelligence (5 Nov 2026), hosted by Claudia: US voters turning down data centres in nearly every local vote and electing governors who promised a pause, Tencent's Hy4 that can see and use a computer, Anthropic's FlashProve, OpenAI buying Pierre, AMD's surge, Elon Musk's data-centres-in-space post, Nvidia's China chip shortfall, Singapore's scam-warning app, Apple's AI arriving in China, a Brazilian court's order to Meta, Uber's four AI-agent rides, Xiaomi's 8-hour robot shift and a robot-run Shanghai store, with captions, sources and screenshots of the news articles.

stories.title: US data centres lost nearly every one of about 40 local ballot votes
stories.summary: On election night, opponents of data centres won virtually all of about 40 local ballot measures across 10 states, preliminary results show. Seven towns passed outright bans on new ones; in Alhambra, California, 82% voted for a ban.

predictions.note: Voters in about 40 local ballot measures across 10 states moved to ban or limit data centres; the fights are still local, not yet national.
Almost a quarter of voters told NBC's exit poll that data centres were crucial to their vote in the 2026 midterms.

stories.title: Texas and Georgia elected governors who campaigned for data-centre moratoriums
stories.summary: Voters elected Gina Hinojosa in Texas and Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, two of the biggest data-centre hubs; both campaigned for moratoriums on new data centres, Wired reports.

predictions.note: Governors-elect in two of the biggest US data-centre hubs campaigned for moratoriums: a state-level step, not yet national policy.

stories.title: Tencent's Hy4 adds vision and computer use, and helped tune training for smaller models
stories.summary: Tencent's new Hy4 model can understand images and operate a computer for the first time, trained on software such as Blender and CAD. Tencent says Hy4 optimised the pre-training setup for its smaller models; weights are due in the coming days.

predictions.note: Tencent says Hy4 optimised the pre-training setup for its smaller models, a company claim of AI helping build AI, with no measured speed-up.

stories.title: Anthropic shares FlashProve, a way to prove which AI model wrote an answer
stories.summary: Anthropic's open-source FlashProve research checks an output against a model's published 'fingerprint' to prove which model produced it, like an email signature, without revealing the model's weights. There are no plans yet to deploy it.

stories.title: OpenAI is buying Pierre, a developer tools start-up, in what Axios calls a move on GitHub
stories.summary: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, whose code storage tools are already built into Codex. Axios, which broke the news, says the deal targets Microsoft's GitHub.

stories.title: AMD's revenue jumped 45% as its data centre sales nearly doubled
stories.summary: AMD's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $13.38 billion and its data centre sales nearly doubled from a year earlier. It forecast about $17 billion for the fourth quarter.

stories.title: Data-centre stocks slid on the election results; Musk eyed space instead
stories.summary: AI data-centre stocks fell as the Texas governor's race and the wider results came in, CNBC reported. Elon Musk posted: 'Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now.'

stories.title: Chinese firms reportedly ordered 6 million Nvidia chips but expect about 1% soon
stories.summary: Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and others have ordered about 6 million Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 chips, worth about $70 billion, but expect only roughly 1% within four months, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar.

stories.title: Singapore's AntiScam Pango, built with Google DeepMind, warns of scam messages live
stories.summary: GovTech Singapore and Google DeepMind launched AntiScam Pango, an Android app that checks WhatsApp, Telegram and SMS messages on the phone itself and warns users in real time when a conversation looks like a scam.

stories.title: Apple Intelligence reaches mainland China in a test version, built with Alibaba's Qwen
stories.summary: Apple's iOS 27.3 developer beta gives users in mainland China their first test access to Apple Intelligence, integrated with Alibaba's Qwen; it is due for everyone with iOS 27.3 in December.

stories.title: A São Paulo court ordered Meta to stop training its AI on Brazilian news outlets' content
stories.summary: In a preliminary injunction, a São Paulo state court told Meta to stop collecting content from outlets in three national press associations to train its AI, with a daily fine of one million reais if it doesn't comply.

stories.title: Uber says outside AI agents booked just four rides last quarter
stories.summary: Only four Uber rides were arranged by third-party AI agents in the third quarter, the company said on its earnings call. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi: 'It is just very, very early.'

stories.title: Xiaomi showed two humanoid robots working a full 8-hour shift in its car factory
stories.summary: Xiaomi posted a time-lapse of two of its humanoid robots working a full shift at a sorting station in its car factory; Electrek notes key numbers such as speed and interventions are missing.

predictions.note: Two humanoid robots worked one full shift at a sorting station in Xiaomi's own factory: a company demo, far short of thousands on live lines.

stories.title: Six AgiBot humanoids ran a Shanghai convenience store for 24 hours; four passed
stories.summary: AgiBot's six G2 robots worked a Shanghai convenience store for a day, completing 1,730 tasks including 147 coffees. Only four passed; the cleaning robot found a full bin on night duty and strayed outside the store.

transcript.t: Welcome to the Singularity Daily, Thursday edition.
Here's what happened in superintelligence in the last 24 hours.
We get a say. America voted, and data centres lost nearly all of about 40 local votes.
Texas and Georgia also elected governors who campaigned to pause new data centres.
Over in China, Tencent's newest AI model can now see, and use a computer too.
Tencent says it already tuned the training setup for its smaller siblings.
AI, improving AI.
Anthropic showed how to prove which AI wrote an answer.
Think of it as a signature.
And OpenAI's buying Pierre, a developer tools start-up.
Axios calls it a shot at GitHub.
Now, the money. AMD's revenue jumped 45%, and its data centre business nearly doubled.
Data centre stocks slid. Elon Musk posted, "Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now."
Meanwhile, Chinese tech giants have reportedly ordered 6 million Nvidia chips.
About $70 billion worth.
Their own guess? They'll get about 1% of them in the next four months.
In Singapore, a new app built with Google DeepMind warns you about scam messages as they arrive.
And Apple's AI finally reached China, in a test version, with help from Alibaba's Qwen.
The catch? A Brazilian court told Meta to stop training on local news.
And Uber says AI agents booked just four rides last quarter. Four.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Now, the machines.
Xiaomi showed two humanoid robots working a full 8-hour shift in its car factory.
In Shanghai, six robots ran a convenience store for a full day, making 147 coffees.
Only four passed probation. The cleaner found a full bin and wandered outside.
So yes, the machines keep clocking in. But we still get a say in how.
Every day, the curve gets a little steeper.
Check the board: the future is running early.
That was 24 hours. Tomorrow will be faster.
That's the Singularity Daily for today.
Stay curious. See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
